question.problem:
$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)=\{\begin{aligned}2y, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=1]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{Y|1}=\frac{2}{3}.$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\textrm{Var}\big[X \,|\, Y=-2\big]$ given that the conditional probability density function $f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, -2)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is $\mu_{X|-2}=\dfrac{3}{4}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\textrm{E}\big[X^2 \,| \, Y=y \big] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 \, f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, y) \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=-2] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3{x}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=-2] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=-2]-{\mu }_{X|-2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}-{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}-\frac{9}{16} \\  & =\frac{3}{80}.\end{aligned}
$$
